statement: A point $P(x,y)$ moves so that its distance from $(a,0)$ is twice its distance from the origin. (i) Show that $P$ lies on a circle and find its centre and radius. (ii) Sketch the locus.
solution: (i) $(x-a)^{2}+y^{2}=4(x^{2}+y^{2})$ gives $3x^{2}+3y^{2}+2ax-a^{2}=0$, i.e. $(x+a/3)^{2}+y^{2}=(2a/3)^{2}$. So it is a circle with centre $(-a/3,0)$ and radius $2a/3$ (for $a>0$). (ii) It is the circle centred at $(-a/3,0)$ passing through the origin and $(-a,0)$.
hints: Write the distance condition as an equation.
